newsitem.title: USA: Strategic main unit won't show Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: Strategic main unit won't show Q1 profit.

text.p: Strategic Distribution Inc said on Monday its main unit, In-Plant Stores, would not show a profit in the first quarter.

The company also said in a statement that president Theodore Rieple would retire and it would buy Houston's INTERMAT International Materials Management Engineers Inc, with the purchase done by the end of January.

The company will buy Intermat for $10.8 million in cash, a $1.4 million subordinated note and 625,000 newly issued shares of Strategic Distribution common stock. Intermat is a provider of inventory cataloguing products.

Board chairman Andrew Bursky said: "Revenue levels at some of our more mature In-Plant Stores have not met our expectations, due to weaker business conditions for these customers. Also, gross margins at some of our newer In-Plant Stores have not achieved budgeted levels..."

"As a result, while our In-Plant Store business performed in line with our expectations for the fourth quarter of 1996, we currently expect that this business will not be profitable in the first quarter of 1997, as we previously had expected," he added.
Strategic Distribution's In-Plant Store program had revenues of $61.7 million for the first nine months of 1996.
Rieple, the president, "has expressed a desire to devote his full attention to the successful divestiture of Strategic Supply and to retire" when the sale is completed, the statement said.
Strategic Distribution plans to sell its Strategic Supply Inc and American Technical Services Group Inc units this year.
